entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The German Revolution of 1918–1919 was a pivotal event in modern history that took place in Germany between 1918-19. It was a revolution that occurred in the midst of World War I, as the German Empire began to collapse under the weight of military defeat and economic hardship. The revolution was sparked by the German people's growing discontent with the monarchy and the war effort, and it ultimately led to the abdication of Kaiser Wilhelm II on November 9, 1918.

The revolution was a complex and multifaceted event, involving not only the overthrow of the monarchy but also the rise of the Weimar Republic, which would go on to shape German politics for decades to come. The revolution was marked by widespread protests, demonstrations, and violence, as well as the formation of workers' councils and other radical organizations. The event was a turning point in German history, marking the end of the imperial era and the beginning of a new era of democracy and social change.

The German Revolution of 1918–1919 had a profound impact on the course of world history, shaping the development of modern Germany and influencing the broader trajectory of European politics. It also had a lasting impact on the lives of ordinary people, from the soldiers who fought in World War I to the workers who formed the backbone of the revolution. As one historian noted, 'The German Revolution of 1918–1919 was a moment of great hope and great uncertainty, a time when the very foundations of society seemed to be shifting beneath the feet of the people.'
